cohort: 312 mothers and their neonates (106 cases with neonatal jaundice and 206 controls without neonatal jaundice) recruited from two governmental hospitals in north Jordan.
finding: Maternal higher education, employment, and caesarean section, as well as neonatal prematurity, fewer than 5 feeds per day, and ABO incompatibility were associated with a higher risk of neonatal jaundice.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was associated with a higher risk of neonatal jaundice.
gest_age: Preterm neonates were included, though specific gestational ages were not reported.
